seasonsNote: Each map zone is a duck zone (Zone 1, Low Plains Zone 2, High Plains Zone 2, Zone 3) and a dark goose unit (North Central, Platte River, Niobrara). White-fronted and light geese, teal, and the light goose conservation order (East, West and Rainwater Basin zones) are statewide or by their own zones listed in the notes.

bags.detail: Tier I: six ducks (mergansers included) with sex and species limits — no more than 5 mallards (2 hens), 3 wood ducks, 3 pintails, 2 redheads, 2 canvasbacks, 1 scaup. Tier II: three ducks of any species and sex. Possession three times the daily bag.
Mergansers count in the duck limit.

rules.d: 30 minutes before sunrise to sunset (NGPC zone layers).
Hunters choose Tier I (six ducks with restrictions) or Tier II (three ducks, any species and sex) when they buy their permit.

Nebraska’s game refuges are closed to hunting; Lake Babcock, Enders Reservoir and Wanamaker are waterfowl or all-hunting closures, and part of Kiowa WMA is closed to all access from Oct 1 until the dark goose season ends. They are the red areas on the map.

rules.d: A 300-acre area with 10 pit blinds, open to waterfowl hunting from the Monday before Thanksgiving to the end of dark goose season; check in at the station and hunt only from the blinds (NGPC waterfowl page). Not drawn.
